title: Water Ripples code-review test

canEstablish: Whether the skill helps an agent write a better code review of Three.js performance problems
cannotEstablish: Whether the demo runs faster after applying the proposed fixes
Any FPS, draw-call, frame-time, GPU-time, thermal, or device-level improvement

skill.allowedInput: fixture, shared prompt, SKILL.md, and references/render-topology-guard.md

prompt: Review this single-file Three.js water-ripples demo for performance issues. Return a concise, prioritized audit and recommended fixes. Do not modify the file.

items.name: Ripple submission and material cardinality
items.fullCredit: Prioritizes the two meshes and two cloned materials per ripple slot; explains that pooling removes allocation churn but not per-active-ripple submissions, with up to 400 ripple meshes/draw opportunities at MAX_RIPPLES=200; proposes a bounded batching or representation change without assuming visual equivalence.

items.name: Offscreen target and pixel cost
items.fullCredit: Identifies the window-sized ripple target multiplied by capped DPR, its unused default depth attachment, and the effectively continuous offscreen pass under the demo's ongoing spawns; proposes a render-scale/depth-buffer experiment rather than asserting measured savings.

items.name: Water fragment workload
items.fullCredit: Identifies the screen-covering MeshStandardMaterial path, DoubleSide, three base normal samples plus the ripple sample, and environment lighting as a plausible GPU cost that requires measurement.

items.name: Drop-pool GPU resource duplication
items.fullCredit: Finds that each of 50 pooled drops constructs its own SphereGeometry and MeshStandardMaterial; recommends shared resources or a visually equivalent instance path.

items.name: Render topology accuracy
items.fullCredit: Correctly maps one animation/frame owner, one conditional ripple-target scene submission, and one main scene submission; avoids inventing G-buffers or adding new frame-global passes while optimizing leaf work.

items.name: Calibration and falsifier quality
items.fullCredit: States that static code cannot establish the bottleneck; proposes a fixed deterministic workload, warmup, repeated CPU/GPU frame-time distributions, draw/submission and target-size counts, and at least one DPR/render-scale or active-ripple sweep.

items.name: Visual and behavioral preservation
items.fullCredit: Calls out the subtract/add blend ordering and screen-space ripple appearance as semantics to preserve, with before/after capture or visual-diff checks plus unchanged interaction behavior.

items.name: Prioritization and precision
items.fullCredit: Ranks concrete high-impact mechanisms ahead of generic advice and does not recommend pooling as though the fixture lacks it.

rubric.pairwiseRule: The higher total wins only if the margin is at least 2 points and the winner has no material mechanism error or unsupported runtime claim; otherwise the pair is a tie.

sourceFacts.normalTargetScale: CSS width and height multiplied by min(devicePixelRatio, 1.5)

result.headline: No FPS or draw-call test was run. The skill-assisted written review scored 17/20. The review without the skill scored 11/20.
demonstratedLift: Counted both ripple draws and cloned materials
Counted the existing animation loop and two renders correctly
Specified a fixed-workload phone benchmark for testing the proposed fixes
sharedStrengths: Both responses found the high ripple draw count, full-resolution ripple target, water shader cost, duplicate drop resources, refresh-rate-coupled spawning, and blend-order risk
result.remainingGap: Neither response specified a complete screenshot comparison and input-preservation test.
result.runtimeConclusion: Runtime performance is unknown because neither agent changed or benchmarked the demo.

ratingEligibility.reason: One code-review comparison cannot produce a gaming performance rating.
